title: Range of a Square-Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For the natural domain of f(x)=sqrt(x-1), determine the set of all output values.

steps.title: Note the Radicand Range
steps.explanation: On the natural domain x >= 1, the inner quantity x-1 sweeps out every nonnegative number.
steps.why: Shifting the domain [1, infinity) left by 1 produces [0, infinity).

steps.title: Apply the Principal Root
steps.explanation: The principal square root returns only nonnegative values, starting at sqrt(0)=0.
steps.why: By convention sqrt denotes the nonnegative root.

steps.title: Confirm Surjectivity onto [0, infinity)
steps.explanation: Any desired output y >= 0 is produced by choosing x=y^2+1, so no nonnegative value is missed.
steps.why: Solving sqrt(x-1)=y for x exhibits a preimage for every candidate output.

steps.title: State the Range
steps.explanation: The outputs are exactly the nonnegative reals, including 0 at x=1.
steps.why: Zero is attained, negative values are impossible, and all positives are hit.
